showcase.summary: A Jupiter-sized planet on a 3.3-day orbit: deep, easy transits, in the TESS southern continuous viewing zone.
showcase.why: The easy case: a transit about 0.6% deep that any search should find, so it shows the whole path from light curve to fit with little doubt about the signal.
showcase.panel_label: Probes only; Sentinels not run on this example

showcase.summary: An M dwarf with three known transiting planets at 3.4, 5.7 and 11.4 days: several periods in one star.
showcase.why: One light curve, three periods. It shows what the search does when a star has more than one planet, and which of them a 13-day subject can hold.
showcase.caveat: Found all 5 of c's transits and both of d's; b not found; d seen twice, no period (one transit per 13-day piece of the light curve).
showcase.outcome_line: TOI-270 b: none of 6 transits; TOI-270 c: 5 of 5 transits (5 candidates); TOI-270 d: 2 of 2 transits (2 flagged; no period).
showcase.panel_label: Probes only; Sentinels not run on this example

showcase.summary: A bright K dwarf with two small known planets: b (about 1.6 Earth radii, 4.8 days, roughly 350 ppm deep) and c (17.2 days).
showcase.why: A small planet whose single transits are near the noise of one sector: it shows what the panel and vetting do at the edge of what a 10-minute-binned search can see, and the page says what it missed.
showcase.caveat: Found 1 of b's 5 transits and both of c's; neither published period was recovered (the BLS period on those dips is not the planet's).
showcase.outcome_line: HD 15337 b: 1 of 5 transits (1 candidate; BLS period not the planet's); HD 15337 c: 2 of 2 transits (1 candidate, 1 flagged; BLS period not the planet's).
showcase.panel_label: Probes only; Sentinels not run on this example

showcase.summary: A TESS Object of Interest the TOI table dispositions as a false positive (FP): a 2.4% dip every 4.5 days.
showcase.why: A test SetuHQ must fail to pass: TOI-236.01 is in the real-TOI benchmark's false-positive set. The page says what the vetting did with it, whatever it did.
showcase.outcome_line: Caught: all 6 dips on the TOI ephemeris were rejected by vetting (secondary_any_phase, secondary_eclipse), so none is a candidate.
showcase.reference: TOI table (NASA Exoplanet Archive): TOI-236.01 dispositioned FP
showcase.panel_label: Probes only; Sentinels not run on this example

showcase.summary: A sun-like star with a super-Earth on a 6.3-day orbit: the run checked in full against Huang et al. 2018.
showcase.why: The reference check: the one run with the Sentinels as well as the Probes, its limb-darkened fit compared with the discovery paper in docs/results/pi_men_validation.md.
showcase.outcome_line: Rp/R★ and T14 within 5% of Huang et al. 2018 (docs/results/pi_men_validation.md).
